## Analysis and substantive alternative

**Simple baseline:** construct donor-level pseudobulk expression from the prepared feature-by-sample matrix, check its lineage and count semantics, and estimate a remission-versus-resistant contrast using a prespecified count model with donor as unit. Report per-gene effects/FDR and a sample-level total-expression contrast using a fixed, reproducible representation; show each donor, age sensitivity and sequencing-run/library sensitivity. Do not treat cells, genes or SDRF lanes as independent replicates. Maximum effective n is 13, so donor bootstrap intervals and leave-one-donor-out influence are essential; narrow covariate models are not credible at this n.

**Mechanistic alternative on the same question:** fit an unsupervised, donor-aware macrophage-state mixture model to the 13 original sparse cell matrices, learning a shared set of states without using remission/resistance labels. In leave-one-donor-out folds, learn state representations on other donors and project the held-out donor; keep all cells from one donor together. Estimate donor-level state fractions and state-specific expression, then decompose total group contrast into captured-state proportion and within-shared-state components using a common reference state distribution. Evaluate cluster/program stability across donor-held-out fits and donor-cluster bootstrap uncertainty. This can reveal a compositional explanation masked by sample averages, which the baseline cannot separate from within-state change. It is exploratory and requires common states and crossed processing/run structure; if states are unstable or group and technical batch are aliased, stop and mark inconclusive. No clinical prediction model or random-cell split is warranted.

Resource plan: baseline CPU 2 cores/8 GiB, estimated under 30 minutes (not benchmarked). Cell-state decomposition CPU 4 cores/16 GiB, estimated 1–2 hours for sparse donor-held-out fits and 1,000 donor bootstrap replicates (unmeasured, package-dependent); no GPU is scientifically useful at this size. Solver planning envelope <=16 CPU, 32 GiB RAM, <=4 hours. These estimates are future workload estimates, not measured discovery results. Discovery performed source/schema inspection only; no transcriptomic analysis or model fit was run.

## Falsification and outcome interpretation

Support for the directional composition hypothesis requires (a) donor-level remission/resistant total expression contrast, (b) reproducibly different proportions of shared, stable macrophage states, and (c) the within-state standardized contrast materially attenuated relative to the total contrast, without a single donor or observed run/lane pattern accounting for the result. This is cross-sectional association only.

- **Supportive:** the total contrast is mainly accounted for by state proportions; standardized within-state effects are smaller and uncertain; learned states are stable in donor-held-out fits. Prioritize orthogonal validation of the captured-state composition explanation, not whole-tissue abundance or causality.
- **Adverse:** stable shared states show a precise within-state contrast that is not attenuated by standardization, while state fractions are similar; this weakens the composition-dominant hypothesis and prioritizes independent perturbation of state regulation.
- **Inconclusive:** wide donor-level uncertainty, unstable clusters, no common states, sensitivity to a single donor, unmeasured group/run alias, poor gene/barcode alignment, or unresolved labels. This is not evidence that states are equivalent.

Falsification requires adequate cell/gene coverage, stable common-state assignment and a precise within-state component not materially attenuated by proportion standardization; otherwise claim only failure to resolve. Computationally checkable: sample/donor flow, joins, matrix alignment, state-fit stability, group contrasts, decomposition, uncertainty and whether conclusions match outputs. Expert adjudication needed for remission/resistance definitions, medications, severity, biopsy context, sequencing/capture confounding, and biological relevance of inferred states. Longitudinal persistence/transition requires prospective repeated samples; whole-tissue abundance/spatial effects require unsorted or spatial data; causality and intervention relevance require perturbation and functional outcomes; clinical treatment selection requires prospective external validation.

## Three inspected key works

[K1] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” *Nature Medicine* (2020), DOI `10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8`. The inspected abstract reports 32,000 STMs, remission-associated MerTK-positive subsets, and different cluster frequencies across clinical states. This is closely related prior work and likely overlaps this dataset; it constrains novelty and does not constitute independent replication. Abstract and limited article context inspected, not full methods/supplements. Attached excerpt: `references/episode2/K1-alivernini-abstract.txt`.

[K2] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” *Science Translational Medicine* (2019), DOI `10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587`. The inspected abstract supports macrophage heterogeneity, stromal conditioning, and a distinct inflammatory macrophage-to-fibroblast path as a serious biological rival. Full-text acquisition was unavailable; abstract only. Attached excerpt: `references/episode2/K2-kuo-abstract.txt`.

[K3] Richard JB et al. “Synovial matrix turnover controls immune cell spatial patterning in inflammation resolution.” *Molecular Systems Biology* (2025), DOI `10.1038/s44320-025-00149-7`. The inspected abstract reports fibroblast/myeloid matrix interactions and collagen-VI-associated spatial immune ingress, reinforcing that proportions in isolated macrophages cannot resolve spatial/stromal causes. Abstract only. Attached excerpt: `references/episode2/K3-richard-abstract.txt`.

## Unchosen alternatives and revision gates

D3-M1's broad whole-tissue composition question is not answerable from macrophage-only expression; the learned cell-state decomposition is a narrower, measured version. D3-M3 transition/persistence claims remain blocked by the cross-sectional single sample. Episode-1 MERTK/FLS UNC1062 study remains separate context and is not an independent validation dataset for this question. E-MTAB-8316/E-MTAB-8873/GSE95588 remain configured and accessible, but their distinct assay populations and donor namespaces are not joined here. Historical EHR demonstrations are not adapted because the molecular sources do not contain longitudinal EHR diagnoses, dates or outcomes.

Revisit/defer if K1 full text/supplements already resolve the same within-state decomposition; if exact remission/resistance criteria and medications cannot be reconciled; if run/batch is perfectly confounded with group; or if held-out state mapping is unstable. A supportive result warrants only orthogonal state-composition validation; another study is required for causal claims.

## New scientific deliverable

The solver must newly fit the donor-level expression contrast and, if identity/batch/stability prerequisites pass, the donor-held-out cell-state mixture decomposition. Completion outputs: cohort flow and exclusions, source scale/lineage QC, per-donor expression/state fractions, total and state-standardized contrast estimates with donor-level uncertainty, held-out state stability, sensitivity results, and an interpretation classified supportive/adverse/inconclusive and justified from these outputs. No reference solution or discovery result is claimed.

Temporal target is one cross-sectional biopsy/library per donor. There is no donor-specific date, pre/post-treatment measure, treatment start/stop time, remission duration, or clinical outcome time field in the inspected design. `treatment` is null for these group records. Source label definitions, medication class/dose/duration, biopsy activity scores, concomitant steroids and detailed batch/capture context require source-record or clinician adjudication.

## Analysis and substantive alternative

**Simple baseline:** construct donor-level pseudobulk expression from the prepared feature-by-sample matrix, check its lineage and count semantics, and estimate a remission-versus-resistant contrast using a prespecified count model with donor as unit. Report per-gene effects/FDR and a sample-level total-expression contrast using a fixed, reproducible representation; show each donor, age sensitivity and sequencing-run/library sensitivity. Do not treat cells, genes or SDRF lanes as independent replicates. Maximum effective n is 13, so donor bootstrap intervals and leave-one-donor-out influence are essential; narrow covariate models are not credible at this n.

**Mechanistic alternative on the same question:** fit an unsupervised, donor-aware macrophage-state mixture model to the 13 original sparse cell matrices, learning a shared set of states without using remission/resistance labels. In leave-one-donor-out folds, learn state representations on other donors and project the held-out donor; keep all cells from one donor together. Estimate donor-level state fractions and state-specific expression, then decompose total group contrast into captured-state proportion and within-shared-state components using a common reference state distribution. Evaluate cluster/program stability across donor-held-out fits and donor-cluster bootstrap uncertainty. This can reveal a compositional explanation masked by sample averages, which the baseline cannot separate from within-state change. It is exploratory and requires common states and crossed processing/run structure; if states are unstable or group and technical batch are aliased, stop and mark inconclusive. No clinical prediction model or random-cell split is warranted.

Resource plan: baseline CPU 2 cores/8 GiB, estimated under 30 minutes (not benchmarked). Cell-state decomposition CPU 4 cores/16 GiB, estimated 1–2 hours for sparse donor-held-out fits and 1,000 donor bootstrap replicates (unmeasured, package-dependent); no GPU is scientifically useful at this size. Solver planning envelope <=16 CPU, 32 GiB RAM, <=4 hours. These estimates are future workload estimates, not measured discovery results. Discovery performed source/schema inspection only; no transcriptomic analysis or model fit was run.

## Falsification and outcome interpretation

Support for the directional composition hypothesis requires (a) donor-level remission/resistant total expression contrast, (b) reproducibly different proportions of shared, stable macrophage states, and (c) the within-state standardized contrast materially attenuated relative to the total contrast, without a single donor or observed run/lane pattern accounting for the result. This is cross-sectional association only.

- **Supportive:** the total contrast is mainly accounted for by state proportions; standardized within-state effects are smaller and uncertain; learned states are stable in donor-held-out fits. Prioritize orthogonal validation of the captured-state composition explanation, not whole-tissue abundance or causality.
- **Adverse:** stable shared states show a precise within-state contrast that is not attenuated by standardization, while state fractions are similar; this weakens the composition-dominant hypothesis and prioritizes independent perturbation of state regulation.
- **Inconclusive:** wide donor-level uncertainty, unstable clusters, no common states, sensitivity to a single donor, unmeasured group/run alias, poor gene/barcode alignment, or unresolved labels. This is not evidence that states are equivalent.

Falsification requires adequate cell/gene coverage, stable common-state assignment and a precise within-state component not materially attenuated by proportion standardization; otherwise claim only failure to resolve. Computationally checkable: sample/donor flow, joins, matrix alignment, state-fit stability, group contrasts, decomposition, uncertainty and whether conclusions match outputs. Expert adjudication needed for remission/resistance definitions, medications, severity, biopsy context, sequencing/capture confounding, and biological relevance of inferred states. Longitudinal persistence/transition requires prospective repeated samples; whole-tissue abundance/spatial effects require unsorted or spatial data; causality and intervention relevance require perturbation and functional outcomes; clinical treatment selection requires prospective external validation.

## Three inspected key works

[K1] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” *Nature Medicine* (2020), DOI `10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8`. The inspected abstract reports 32,000 STMs, remission-associated MerTK-positive subsets, and different cluster frequencies across clinical states. This is closely related prior work and likely overlaps this dataset; it constrains novelty and does not constitute independent replication. Abstract and limited article context inspected, not full methods/supplements. Attached excerpt: `references/episode2/K1-alivernini-abstract.txt`.

[K2] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” *Science Translational Medicine* (2019), DOI `10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587`. The inspected abstract supports macrophage heterogeneity, stromal conditioning, and a distinct inflammatory macrophage-to-fibroblast path as a serious biological rival. Full-text acquisition was unavailable; abstract only. Attached excerpt: `references/episode2/K2-kuo-abstract.txt`.

[K3] Richard JB et al. “Synovial matrix turnover controls immune cell spatial patterning in inflammation resolution.” *Molecular Systems Biology* (2025), DOI `10.1038/s44320-025-00149-7`. The inspected abstract reports fibroblast/myeloid matrix interactions and collagen-VI-associated spatial immune ingress, reinforcing that proportions in isolated macrophages cannot resolve spatial/stromal causes. Abstract only. Attached excerpt: `references/episode2/K3-richard-abstract.txt`.

D3-M1's broad whole-tissue composition question is not answerable from macrophage-only expression; the learned cell-state decomposition is a narrower, measured version. D3-M3 transition/persistence claims remain blocked by the cross-sectional single sample. Episode-1 MERTK/FLS UNC1062 study remains separate context and is not an independent validation dataset for this question. E-MTAB-8316/E-MTAB-8873/GSE95588 remain configured and accessible, but their distinct assay populations and donor namespaces are not joined here. Historical EHR demonstrations are not adapted because the molecular sources do not contain longitudinal EHR diagnoses, dates or outcomes.

Revisit/defer if K1 full text/supplements already resolve the same within-state decomposition; if exact remission/resistance criteria and medications cannot be reconciled; if run/batch is perfectly confounded with group; or if held-out state mapping is unstable. A supportive result warrants only orthogonal state-composition validation; another study is required for causal claims.

## New scientific deliverable

The solver must newly fit the donor-level expression contrast and, if identity/batch/stability prerequisites pass, the donor-held-out cell-state mixture decomposition. Completion outputs: cohort flow and exclusions, source scale/lineage QC, per-donor expression/state fractions, total and state-standardized contrast estimates with donor-level uncertainty, held-out state stability, sensitivity results, and an interpretation classified supportive/adverse/inconclusive and justified from these outputs. No reference solution or discovery result is claimed.

# Do remission-associated macrophage averages reflect captured state representation?

## Scientific question and deliverable

**Question:** Among rheumatoid-arthritis synovial membrane macrophages sampled once in E-MTAB-8322, does the observed remission-versus-treatment-resistant average-expression contrast have a robust, estimable component attributable to differences in captured macrophage expression-state proportions, or is within-state expression change at least as large?

**Falsifiable hypothesis (untested):** Conditional on a technical-overlap gate, more than half of the squared multigene remission/resistant macrophage-expression distance is attributable to state-proportion differences rather than state-conditional expression differences, and that attribution is stable to donor resampling and leave-one-donor-out state fitting. The 50% threshold defines “dominant” before any analysis. Composition and within-state regulation may coexist. Here “state” means a reproducible expression cluster inferred in this assay, not a stable lineage, transition, or mechanism.

**Clinical importance:** An average synovial signature alone can motivate the wrong next experiment. If state representation robustly accounts for most of this cross-sectional contrast, prioritize measuring recruitment/retention and tissue localization in a follow-up study; if within-state expression dominates, prioritize targeted cell perturbation or functional testing. If the decomposition is unidentifiable or unstable, stop and obtain clinical, spatial, or technical evidence before choosing either direction. No result alone selects or changes a patient’s treatment.

## Evidence-supported and unresolved claims

**Strongest evidence-supported claim:** The inspected literature reports synovial macrophage heterogeneity and remission-associated macrophage observations [K1], describes HBEGF+ macrophage–fibroblast invasiveness as a plausible within-state/tissue-crosstalk alternative [K2], and reports a spatial LYVE1+ macrophage network associated with treatment response in another, spatial and longitudinal study [K3]. These works support biological plausibility and important boundary conditions. K1–K3 were inspected at abstract level only; no full text or supplementary methods are claimed here.

**Untested claim:** Whether the average expression contrast in the specifically bound 13 E-MTAB-8322 RA donors is quantitatively dominated by captured-state proportions rather than expression conditional on state, after testing whether donor status is entangled with available technical structure. E-MTAB-8322 provides a one-time macrophage-only assay. This analysis is a descriptive decomposition, not a causal or treatment-effect estimate, not independent replication, and not evidence of cell transition. The source study may overlap the closest remission literature [K1]; this proposal does not claim novelty of remission-associated macrophage subsets or that the decomposition has never been reported in its detailed source article.

**Strongest rival and artifacts:** Within-state transcriptional regulation is the direct biological rival, and can coexist with a composition effect. A potentially more fundamental rival is that status groups differ in current disease severity, therapy class or history, biopsy selection, cell recovery/capture, or sequencing/library structure. These factors could alter both the measured state proportions and mean expression. The prepared annotation has an empty/null `treatment` field and does not provide disease-activity scores or longitudinal clinical records; statistical adjustment cannot repair those absences. Spatial fibroblast/vascular niches are also unmeasured. Even an adjusted or stable association would not identify a mechanism.

## Exact population, data, joins, and time boundary

Snapshot is `core-molecular-20261003`. The binding template/source catalog is `datasets/disease_mechanisms/README.md` and `datasets/disease_mechanisms/metadata.json`; the assay registry is `[private-path]/assay-registry.json` (SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`). Source files are read-only.

**Primary population:** 13 verified RA synovial membrane macrophage donors: remission n=7 (SA132, SA159, SA160, SA161, SA168, SA174, SA225) and treatment-resistant n=6 (SA144, SA145, SA151, SA166, SA222, SA227), as verified in the parent’s source reconciliation of the sample design and SDRF. Do not include healthy, untreated/naive RA, undifferentiated arthritis, or SA149/SA149P related-or-repeated identity records in this primary contrast. One donor is the independent unit; cells and sequencing runs are not independent biological replicates.

**Prepared profile and annotations:** `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz` (SHA-256 `95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36`) has feature-by-sample expression (`feature` row identifier, sample IDs as columns; 33,694 feature rows and 27 samples per assay registry). `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json` (SHA-256 `4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da`) has 27 sample records and fields `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `other_donor_id`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata`, `source_name`, and `cells`. Join matrix columns to `sample_id` exactly. Filter verified rows on `tissue='synovial membrane'`, `cell_type='macrophage'`, RA disease and remission/resistance response; verify rather than infer from abbreviated labels. Preserve the prepared table for simple baseline only after checking its transformation/scale; it has no cell-state assignments.

**Primary single-cell inputs for decomposition:** For each of the 13 named donor prefixes, use the exact source trio `[private-path]/{prefix}.matrix.mtx`, `{prefix}.genes.tsv`, and `{prefix}.barcodes.tsv`, where prefixes are `RemSA132`, `RemSA159`, `RemSA160`, `RemSA161`, `RemSA168`, `RemSA174`, `RemSA225`, `ResistantSA144`, `ResistantSA145`, `ResistantSA151`, `ResistantSA166`, `ResistantSA222`, and `ResistantSA227`. The MEX-like sparse matrix is genes/features by cells; matrix row i maps to row i of that donor’s `genes.tsv`, and column j maps to row j of its `barcodes.tsv`. Use the same donor identity for all three files; do not join unrelated dataset ID namespaces. Verify matrix orientation, count scale, dimensions and feature concordance against source files before fitting. These are the assay’s available cell profiles, not a download of FASTQ/BAM or spatial data. No cluster labels are available in the bound files; infer them as part of the alternative.

**Run/protocol reconciliation and time boundary:** `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.sdrf.txt` (SHA-256 `b87005a9eefff1beb2d12de2e9f945e2a0b6330aa59207f61f0ecaba180fa237`) is a 106-row run-level design with columns including `Source Name`, `Characteristics[individual]`, `Characteristics[disease]`, `Characteristics[response to treatment]`, `Characteristics[age]`, `Characteristics[sex]`, `Characteristics[organism part]`, `Characteristics[cell type]`, `Characteristics[disease staging]`, `Technology Type`, `Comment[ENA_EXPERIMENT]`, `Scan Name`, `Comment[ENA_RUN]`, `Comment[LIBRARY_LAYOUT]`, `Comment[LIBRARY_STRATEGY]`, and `Derived Array Data File`. Join its `Source Name` to design `source_name`; cross-check `Characteristics[individual]` and status before comparing runs per donor. These are technical sequencing-run/library records, not independent subjects. `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.idf.txt` (SHA-256 `3755fdf0db73c3dca32e0b4b70aeec2e91df16a737137933de2064aeb1bfe069`) lists experiment metadata and an experiment date of 2018-08-01; there is no per-donor pre/post timeline. Restrict inference to one sampled biopsy per donor and the deposited response labels. Do not analyze change over time or imply treatment caused status.

## Analysis plan and method comparison

First, reconcile donor/status mappings and inspect overlap between response group and observable technical variables (run count, ENA experiment/assay, platform/library fields if variable), along with age, sex, captured-cell yield, and sample-processing descriptors available in the design/SDRF. Show complete donor-level tables and standardized differences rather than relying on a regression coefficient with n=13. Quantify RNA/cell recovery and library-depth dependence. Technical variables that are constant across groups cannot be adjusted; if status is perfectly confounded with an observable processing/run variable, stop biological attribution and report non-identifiability. Cell yields characterize sampling precision, not population abundance in tissue.

**Baseline:** aggregate all captured macrophage expression per donor from the bound single-cell matrix, then estimate remission-minus-resistant differences for common expressed genes after library-size normalization and a fixed variance-stabilizing transformation. Confirm direction and donor influence with the prepared donor profile as a scale/lineage sensitivity check. Use equal donor weighting; uncertainty comes from donor bootstrap and donor-label permutation (up to all 1,716 assignments of 7 labels among 13), never from treating cells as replicates. The baseline determines whether an all-cell average difference is present but cannot say why.

**Alternative selected:** cross-fitted donor-level state decomposition using the original per-cell profiles. In leave-one-donor-out folds, learn low-dimensional structure and macrophage expression-state clusters on the other donors, map the held-out donor’s cells to learned states, and align fold-specific state labels by marker/centroid similarity. Report held-out state assignment and mapping stability; the hypothesis is not interpretable if state maps do not reproduce. Estimate a donor’s state-proportion vector and state-conditional gene profile, then compute standardized group means and the composition-versus-within-state contribution to squared multigene expression distance using symmetric Shapley allocation (the composition-by-expression interaction split equally). Restrict the primary feature set to genes detected in both groups under a label-blind donor/cell prevalence filter fixed before status comparisons. Use identical donors, genes, normalization and equal-donor group weights for baseline and decomposition. Bootstrap and permute donors; report uncertainty and all leave-one-donor-out results. Do not make cell-level significance claims or use learned states as treatment predictors.

The method-comparison rationale, targets, split, uncertainty approach and CPU budget are recorded separately in `method-comparison.md`. The decomposition is selected because it could attribute an observed average difference to two biologically distinct statistical components; no neural embedding or GPU is necessary for this small, donor-limited question. Cross-fitting limits donor leakage but cannot make expression-defined clusters independent of the biological contrast or eliminate capture confounding.

**Estimand and decision rule:** The primary value is the Shapley-attributed fraction of total squared remission/resistant group-mean expression distance assigned to composition. “Composition-dominant” means a point estimate above 0.50 with donor-level uncertainty and held-out state assignment sufficiently stable to support that direction. This threshold is a descriptive criterion, not a clinical decision threshold. Report the component magnitudes as well as the share, because ratios can be unstable if total distance is near zero. Do not silently redefine the gene set, clustering resolution, or split after seeing the desired direction; report sensitivity as exploratory and require any selected alternative to be identified as exploratory.

## Outcomes, falsification, and next decisions

- **Supportive:** technical/status overlap passes the prespecified gate; held-out state mappings and donor influence are stable; the composition share is above 0.50 with donor-level uncertainty supporting a dominant direction. This supports only a cross-sectional decomposition of selected, captured macrophages. Continue to spatial/cell-count validation and clinical adjudication; do not say state abundance causes remission.
- **Adverse:** a precise and stable result assigns at least as much distance to within-state expression as to composition, or the composition result reverses under donor holdout/state mapping checks. This weakens this cohort’s composition-dominant hypothesis and redirects the next study toward validating within-state programs or other measured alternatives. It does not establish a particular pathway or mechanism.
- **Inconclusive/defer:** wide donor-level intervals, low state-map stability, small/near-zero total distance, status/technical non-overlap, dominant donor leverage, or lack of sufficient state support in one group. This means the dataset cannot separate the explanations reliably; it is not decisive evidence for equality or against a biological effect. Obtain better-resolved clinical metadata, independent donor replication, spatial/whole-tissue measurement or a prospective design before advancing.

**Exact evidence needed beyond this analysis:** Clinician review of remission/resistance definitions, assessment date, disease-activity score, drug class/dose/duration and prior treatment trajectory, biopsy indication/selection, and donor-level covariates to distinguish severity and treatment history; independent pathology or spatial measurement to determine whether captured state proportions reflect tissue localization/abundance; and prospective/perturbational evidence to claim state transitions, mechanism, or treatment causality. Computationally checkable outputs include joins/cohort counts, cell/run yield summaries, state-fit reproducibility, effect/decomposition calculations, donor-level uncertainty and whether conclusions follow those outputs. Clinical label validity, unrecorded severity/treatment confounding, mechanisms, and treatment effects require adjudication or another study; an automatic verifier cannot establish them.

## Key references

[K1] Alivernini S, et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” *Nature Medicine* (2020). DOI: 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Abstract-only inspection. The prior supports subset heterogeneity/remission association, not causation or the proposed decomposition. The proposed contribution is an explicit donor-aware component attribution plus technical-overlap gate in the bound contrast.

[K2] Kuo D, et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” *Science Translational Medicine* (2019). DOI: 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only inspection. This supports a within-state and macrophage–fibroblast rival; the present macrophage-only assay cannot establish or localize that crosstalk.

[K3] De Lima J, et al. “Spatial mapping of rheumatoid arthritis synovial niches reveals a LYVE1+ macrophage network associated with response to therapy.” *Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases* (2025). DOI: 10.1016/j.ard.2025.07.019. Abstract-only inspection. This supports spatial/treatment timing as a material boundary; the current single-biopsy profiles cannot test their longitudinal or spatial claims.

# Does the remission–resistance macrophage signal travel across donors?

## Hypothesis and clinical/scientific decision

**Falsifiable hypothesis:** In the cross-sectional E-MTAB-8322 comparison of synovial tissue macrophages from RA donors labelled remission (7 donors) versus treatment-resistant (6 donors), a learned, condition-blind macrophage expression-program decomposition will show a reproducible donor-level composition-versus-within-program split in held-out donors that is not erased by equalizing cell detection depth or omitting individual donors. The stricter primary prediction is that program abundance contributes more than two-thirds of the standardized aggregate expression contrast (defined below). A signal that does not transfer to held-out donors, or that tracks capture/run structure, will contradict this claim.

This is not a hypothesis that a state persists, transitions, or causes remission; one biopsy per donor cannot identify transitions, and the groups were not randomized. It also is not an immediate patient treatment rule. The next decision it can change is research prioritization: a stable composition-dominant association supports a matched spatial/clinical study of niche occupancy; a stable within-program component supports an independent perturbation study of a candidate program; an unstable or technically aliased contrast argues against either mechanistic investment until a better-matched cohort is available. The experiment does not decide whether treatment should be stopped, started, or changed.

## Evidence, unresolved question, closest prior work

**Strongest claim supported by inspected evidence:** Synovial macrophages are heterogeneous and differ across clinical groups. Alivernini et al. report differing frequencies of macrophage clusters and remission-associated MerTK-positive populations, plus functional fibroblast responses [K1]. HBEGF-positive macrophages provide an important counterexample to treating macrophage programs as one simple resolution-to-inflammation axis: that work links an inflammatory macrophage subset to fibroblast invasiveness [K2]. A later spatial study ties a LYVE1-positive macrophage network to perivascular niches and response to therapy, showing why cell-intrinsic expression alone can miss tissue context [K3]. These findings support relevance of macrophage state and niche, not causality of the group contrast in this analysis.

**Unresolved claim tested here:** Do the E-MTAB-8322 remission/resistance differences represent a donor-reproducible separation of program abundance and within-program expression, or do they depend on a few donors, cell capture depth, or sequencing-run structure? This is a robustness and decomposition question, not an assertion that macrophage subsets have not been reported. K1 is closely related and likely overlaps the E-MTAB-8322 source cohort; its abstract already reports cluster-frequency differences. Therefore this proposal is not independent biological replication and makes no novelty claim about those clusters. Its incremental value is to define an explicit, donor-held-out estimand and sensitivity test for whether a composition-versus-within-program interpretation is sufficiently stable to justify which independent experiment comes next.

**Leading explanation and rivals:** A reproducible macrophage program shift may be represented partly by changes in its prevalence and partly by expression changes among cells assigned to that program. The strongest rival is selection/measurement: contemporaneous disease severity and medication history may differ between clinical labels, and tissue dissociation, viable-cell yield, capture depth or sequencing runs may alter detected cell/program composition. These effects could create or amplify the same group contrast. Spatial stromal niches are a second rival/context; single-cell macrophage-only counts cannot resolve them. A donor-level association persisting adjustment or holdout is not proof of intrinsic mechanism. If group and technical variables are aliased, this observational dataset cannot identify which caused the pattern.

## Exact data, population, joins and temporal boundary

Use snapshot `core-molecular-20261003`; source files remain read-only. The assay registry is `[private-path]/assay-registry.json` (SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`), which identifies E-MTAB-8322 as 27 donor/sample profiles and 33,694 measured features. The full dataset file inventory and snapshot lineage are in `datasets/disease_mechanisms/README.md` and the domain `catalog.json`; the assay cards in `domain-guide.md` explicitly warn that the prepared values are macrophage-only pseudobulk and SA149/SA149P identity is unresolved.

- **Primary expression table:** `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz`, tab-separated feature-by-sample counts, `feature` key and sample-ID columns, 33,694 feature rows by 27 sample columns (source SHA-256 `95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36`). Retain original feature IDs; do not treat this as state-resolved or whole-tissue expression.
- **Sample/donor design:** `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json`, 27 records (SHA-256 `4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da`). Required fields: `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `other_donor_id`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_name`, `source_metadata`, `cells`. Matrix sample columns join exactly to `sample_id`; biological replicates are unique `donor_id`, never cells or lanes.

Its `treatment` field is null in the inspected remission/resistant records; the categorical response label is not a medication exposure. The raw UMI matrix/barcodes do not supply cell-level technical run metadata; use the SDRF donor-to-run audit where mapped. Clinical adjudication and lane-level mapping may still be incomplete. ### Estimand and baseline

Target the **captured-cell** difference in normalized macrophage expression between remission and treatment-resistant donors. First reconcile matrix/design/source identities, remove only invalid features/cells using outcome-blind QC, and report per-donor cell counts, total UMIs, detected genes, run counts and distributions. Primary sensitivity includes supplied called cells with valid gene/barcode alignment; repeat after equalizing each donor's cells and detection depth to the minimum support across donors and under frozen low-feature cell filters. Do not interpret cell proportions as intact-tissue abundance.

The simple baseline aggregates each donor's original counts over all retained macrophages (one pseudobulk per donor), applies a count-appropriate normalization and donor-level group contrast, and reports gene-wise effects with donor-label permutation and donor bootstrap intervals. A conventional condition-blind clustering baseline (clusters learned on training donors, held-out cells assigned to cluster centroids) additionally reports each donor's cluster proportions and cluster-stratified pseudobulk effects. This baseline answers whether aggregate expression and discrete cluster fractions reproduce the contrast, but it loses overlapping programs and can conflate a broad state with a within-state shift. Cells do not increase the independent sample size; no cell-level p-values will be treated as donor inference.

Fit an outcome-blind, sparse Poisson/NB low-rank program model to cell-level counts, with donor-specific program weights and gene loadings (candidate program count K=2–6 selected solely within each training split by held-out-donor count reconstruction/stability). To limit overfit and computation, select up to 2,000 variable measured genes using training donors only, retaining the original Ensembl-ID-to-symbol map; project held-out donors onto the frozen training loadings. Donor clinical labels are not used to discover programs. Fit 13 outer leave-one-donor-out folds; align fold programs by loading similarity before comparing weights/loadings. Report held-out reconstruction/deviance and loading/weight stability as adequacy measures, not biological endpoints.

For the donor-level remission-minus-resistant expression vector on the common measured gene set, standardize features by pooled donor-level dispersion and decompose the model-estimated group contrast into program-abundance and within-program terms using a symmetric Oaxaca-style decomposition (split abundance-by-expression interaction equally). Report component vectors and the prespecified relative magnitude

`Q_abundance = ||C_abundance||2 / (||C_abundance||2 + ||C_within||2)`.

This is a relative decomposition magnitude, not a percent of causal effect or variance explained. Define composition/program-abundance dominance as `Q_abundance > 2/3`; within-program dominance as `Q_abundance < 1/3`; intermediate estimates indicate mixed contributions. Compute donor-stratified bootstrap intervals, all 1,716 possible 7-versus-6 donor-label permutations for the aggregate contrast when feasible, leave-one-donor-out estimates, and equal-cell/equal-detection-depth repeats. The alternative can reveal shared co-varying gene programs and whether the same decomposition transfers to unseen donors, which the average pseudobulk signature or non-overlapping hard clusters cannot; it cannot establish a pathway's causality or its function in intact synovium.

**Matched evaluation and uncertainty:** Both approaches use the same remission/resistant donors, held-out donor folds, training-only feature selection, label permutation/bootstrap, and cell-depth sensitivity. Evaluate component direction/magnitude and its fold-to-fold stability; evaluate baseline and learned-model generalization by held-out count deviance and reconstruction. Do not treat better cell-level reconstruction as evidence of clinical importance. Prespecified primary interpretation: support the abundance-dominant hypothesis only if the donor-bootstrap 95% interval for `Q_abundance` lies wholly above 2/3, fold components are reasonably aligned, and equal-depth/leave-one-donor-out analyses do not materially reverse the result. Contradict it if the interval lies wholly below 2/3; a wholly sub-1/3 interval specifically favors within-program dominance. If intervals span 1/3–2/3, the split is mixed/imprecise and is not a falsification of all macrophage biology.

## Alternative selection, split, and compute plan

The baseline and factor model are both donor-aware and directly answer the same decomposition question. The baseline is cheap and transparent; the learned count-factor alternative is selected because correlated, overlapping gene programs and per-donor mixture weights are the substantive uncertainty, not a small classifier score. A scVI-style variational model was considered as a possible way to represent nonlinear cell-level structure, but is deferred: with 13 biological donors, unmeasured clinical/technical confounding and no independent cohort, its extra flexibility would not distinguish those rivals and would complicate program matching. It is not rejected categorically; revisit only if factor-model stability fails for reasons that a held-out learned embedding can resolve and independent donor validation becomes available. Pseudotime/trajectory approaches are not appropriate to these single-time-point data and would not answer the stated question.

**Inputs / target / split / outcome / budget:** Model input is the 13 listed `.matrix.mtx` × `.genes.tsv` × `.barcodes.tsv` triplets plus design/SDRF-derived donor and run mapping; target is held-out count reconstruction and stable factor loadings/weights, then donor-level abundance-vs-within decomposition. Outer split is leave-one-donor-out (13 folds), never cell-random. Inner factor count and HVG selection use training donors only. Evaluate held-out deviance, loading alignment, donor-level component estimate, exact/permutation uncertainty, donor bootstrap, leave-one-donor-out influence and equal-depth sensitivity. Future compute estimate (not measured): CPU 4 cores, 16 GiB RAM, up to 2 hours for sparse 2,000-gene fits, K=2–6 over 13 folds and bootstrap/permutation summaries; no GPU requested because sparse tabular count factorization is the expected workload, not because CUDA is absent. The configured reference timeout is 7,200 seconds; timing remains unverified until solver execution. Do not downscope the cohort or remove folds to meet an unmeasured runtime: if this bound fails, profile sparse fitting and ask the Lead to approve a revised design.

## Falsification, result meanings and next decision

- **Support:** the abundance-dominant estimate passes the pre-registered two-thirds interval rule, learned programs align across held-out donors, and the conclusion survives cell-depth equalization and single-donor removal. This supports a robust cross-sectional captured-macrophage association and justifies a matched, independent spatial cohort to ask whether tissue-level niche occupancy corroborates it; it does not show recruitment, persistence, mechanism, or causality.
- **Adverse to the primary hypothesis:** `Q_abundance` is confidently below 2/3 or the apparent group signal is unstable, reverses with donor holdout/depth sensitivity, or tracks recorded run/cell-yield structure. A confidently sub-1/3 interval specifically supports a within-program rather than abundance-dominant description. If a within-program signature is reproducible, the next useful step is independent matched validation before any perturbation. If technical tracking dominates, revise toward measurement/capture validation and do not nominate a therapeutic target.
- **Inconclusive:** the interval overlaps the 1/3–2/3 region; factors fail to align in held-out folds; there are too few detected cells in one donor; clinical labels/identity cannot be adjudicated; or response and technical factors are aliased. Do not call a wide null/equivalence or refute the biology. Prioritize clinical/run metadata adjudication or a larger matched/spatial cohort before mechanistic claims.

The strongest automatic checks can verify source file/header and matrix dimensions; exact sample–donor–SDRF joins; exclusions; donor-level rather than cell-level inference; train-only feature selection; held-out donor code; reproducible computation of decomposition, intervals and sensitivity outputs; and whether the written conclusion matches those outputs without causal/longitudinal overclaim. An automatic verifier cannot establish clinical remission/resistance validity, unrecorded treatment/severity balance, spatial localization, true independent replication, or a biological mechanism. These require source-clinical adjudication, spatial assay/expert review, or another study.

# Do remission-associated macrophage averages reflect captured state representation?

## Scientific question and deliverable

**Question:** Among rheumatoid-arthritis synovial membrane macrophages sampled once in E-MTAB-8322, does the observed remission-versus-treatment-resistant average-expression contrast have a robust, estimable component attributable to differences in captured macrophage expression-state proportions, or is within-state expression change at least as large?

**Falsifiable hypothesis (untested):** Conditional on a technical-overlap gate, more than half of the squared multigene remission/resistant macrophage-expression distance is attributable to state-proportion differences rather than state-conditional expression differences, and that attribution is stable to donor resampling and leave-one-donor-out state fitting. The 50% threshold defines “dominant” before any analysis. Composition and within-state regulation may coexist. Here “state” means a reproducible expression cluster inferred in this assay, not a stable lineage, transition, or mechanism.

**Clinical importance:** An average synovial signature alone can motivate the wrong next experiment. If state representation robustly accounts for most of this cross-sectional contrast, prioritize measuring recruitment/retention and tissue localization in a follow-up study; if within-state expression dominates, prioritize targeted cell perturbation or functional testing. If the decomposition is unidentifiable or unstable, stop and obtain clinical, spatial, or technical evidence before choosing either direction. No result alone selects or changes a patient’s treatment.

## Evidence-supported and unresolved claims

**Strongest evidence-supported claim:** The inspected literature reports synovial macrophage heterogeneity and remission-associated macrophage observations [K1], describes HBEGF+ macrophage–fibroblast invasiveness as a plausible within-state/tissue-crosstalk alternative [K2], and reports a spatial LYVE1+ macrophage network associated with treatment response in another, spatial and longitudinal study [K3]. These works support biological plausibility and important boundary conditions. K1–K3 were inspected at abstract level only; no full text or supplementary methods are claimed here.

**Untested claim:** Whether the average expression contrast in the specifically bound 13 E-MTAB-8322 RA donors is quantitatively dominated by captured-state proportions rather than expression conditional on state, after testing whether donor status is entangled with available technical structure. E-MTAB-8322 provides a one-time macrophage-only assay. This analysis is a descriptive decomposition, not a causal or treatment-effect estimate, not independent replication, and not evidence of cell transition. The source study may overlap the closest remission literature [K1]; this proposal does not claim novelty of remission-associated macrophage subsets or that the decomposition has never been reported in its detailed source article.

**Strongest rival and artifacts:** Within-state transcriptional regulation is the direct biological rival, and can coexist with a composition effect. A potentially more fundamental rival is that status groups differ in current disease severity, therapy class or history, biopsy selection, cell recovery/capture, or sequencing/library structure. These factors could alter both the measured state proportions and mean expression. The prepared annotation has an empty/null `treatment` field and does not provide disease-activity scores or longitudinal clinical records; statistical adjustment cannot repair those absences. Spatial fibroblast/vascular niches are also unmeasured. Even an adjusted or stable association would not identify a mechanism.

## Exact population, data, joins, and time boundary

Snapshot is `core-molecular-20261003`. The binding template/source catalog is `datasets/disease_mechanisms/README.md` and `datasets/disease_mechanisms/metadata.json`; the assay registry is `[private-path]/assay-registry.json` (SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`). Source files are read-only.

**Primary population:** 13 verified RA synovial membrane macrophage donors: remission n=7 (SA132, SA159, SA160, SA161, SA168, SA174, SA225) and treatment-resistant n=6 (SA144, SA145, SA151, SA166, SA222, SA227), as verified in the parent’s source reconciliation of the sample design and SDRF. Do not include healthy, untreated/naive RA, undifferentiated arthritis, or SA149/SA149P related-or-repeated identity records in this primary contrast. One donor is the independent unit; cells and sequencing runs are not independent biological replicates.

**Prepared profile and annotations:** `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz` (SHA-256 `95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36`) has feature-by-sample expression (`feature` row identifier, sample IDs as columns; 33,694 feature rows and 27 samples per assay registry). `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json` (SHA-256 `4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da`) has 27 sample records and fields `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `other_donor_id`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata`, `source_name`, and `cells`. Join matrix columns to `sample_id` exactly. Filter verified rows on `tissue='synovial membrane'`, `cell_type='macrophage'`, RA disease and remission/resistance response; verify rather than infer from abbreviated labels. Preserve the prepared table for simple baseline only after checking its transformation/scale; it has no cell-state assignments.

**Primary single-cell inputs for decomposition:** For each of the 13 named donor prefixes, use the exact source trio `[private-path]/{prefix}.matrix.mtx`, `{prefix}.genes.tsv`, and `{prefix}.barcodes.tsv`, where prefixes are `RemSA132`, `RemSA159`, `RemSA160`, `RemSA161`, `RemSA168`, `RemSA174`, `RemSA225`, `ResistantSA144`, `ResistantSA145`, `ResistantSA151`, `ResistantSA166`, `ResistantSA222`, and `ResistantSA227`. The MEX-like sparse matrix is genes/features by cells; matrix row i maps to row i of that donor’s `genes.tsv`, and column j maps to row j of its `barcodes.tsv`. Use the same donor identity for all three files; do not join unrelated dataset ID namespaces. Verify matrix orientation, count scale, dimensions and feature concordance against source files before fitting. These are the assay’s available cell profiles, not a download of FASTQ/BAM or spatial data. No cluster labels are available in the bound files; infer them as part of the alternative.

**Run/protocol reconciliation and time boundary:** `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.sdrf.txt` (SHA-256 `b87005a9eefff1beb2d12de2e9f945e2a0b6330aa59207f61f0ecaba180fa237`) is a 106-row run-level design with columns including `Source Name`, `Characteristics[individual]`, `Characteristics[disease]`, `Characteristics[response to treatment]`, `Characteristics[age]`, `Characteristics[sex]`, `Characteristics[organism part]`, `Characteristics[cell type]`, `Characteristics[disease staging]`, `Technology Type`, `Comment[ENA_EXPERIMENT]`, `Scan Name`, `Comment[ENA_RUN]`, `Comment[LIBRARY_LAYOUT]`, `Comment[LIBRARY_STRATEGY]`, and `Derived Array Data File`. Join its `Source Name` to design `source_name`; cross-check `Characteristics[individual]` and status before comparing runs per donor. These are technical sequencing-run/library records, not independent subjects. `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.idf.txt` (SHA-256 `3755fdf0db73c3dca32e0b4b70aeec2e91df16a737137933de2064aeb1bfe069`) lists experiment metadata and an experiment date of 2018-08-01; there is no per-donor pre/post timeline. Restrict inference to one sampled biopsy per donor and the deposited response labels. Do not analyze change over time or imply treatment caused status.

## Analysis plan and method comparison

First, reconcile donor/status mappings and inspect overlap between response group and observable technical variables (run count, ENA experiment/assay, platform/library fields if variable), along with age, sex, captured-cell yield, and sample-processing descriptors available in the design/SDRF. Show complete donor-level tables and standardized differences rather than relying on a regression coefficient with n=13. Quantify RNA/cell recovery and library-depth dependence. Technical variables that are constant across groups cannot be adjusted; if status is perfectly confounded with an observable processing/run variable, stop biological attribution and report non-identifiability. Cell yields characterize sampling precision, not population abundance in tissue.

**Baseline:** aggregate all captured macrophage expression per donor from the bound single-cell matrix, then estimate remission-minus-resistant differences for common expressed genes after library-size normalization and a fixed variance-stabilizing transformation. Confirm direction and donor influence with the prepared donor profile as a scale/lineage sensitivity check. Use equal donor weighting; uncertainty comes from donor bootstrap and donor-label permutation (up to all 1,716 assignments of 7 labels among 13), never from treating cells as replicates. The baseline determines whether an all-cell average difference is present but cannot say why.

**Alternative selected:** cross-fitted donor-level state decomposition using the original per-cell profiles. In leave-one-donor-out folds, learn low-dimensional structure and macrophage expression-state clusters on the other donors, map the held-out donor’s cells to learned states, and align fold-specific state labels by marker/centroid similarity. Report held-out state assignment and mapping stability; the hypothesis is not interpretable if state maps do not reproduce. Estimate a donor’s state-proportion vector and state-conditional gene profile, then compute standardized group means and the composition-versus-within-state contribution to squared multigene expression distance using symmetric Shapley allocation (the composition-by-expression interaction split equally). Restrict the primary feature set to genes detected in both groups under a label-blind donor/cell prevalence filter fixed before status comparisons. Use identical donors, genes, normalization and equal-donor group weights for baseline and decomposition. Bootstrap and permute donors; report uncertainty and all leave-one-donor-out results. Do not make cell-level significance claims or use learned states as treatment predictors.

The method-comparison rationale, targets, split, uncertainty approach and CPU budget are recorded separately in `method-comparison.md`. The decomposition is selected because it could attribute an observed average difference to two biologically distinct statistical components; no neural embedding or GPU is necessary for this small, donor-limited question. Cross-fitting limits donor leakage but cannot make expression-defined clusters independent of the biological contrast or eliminate capture confounding.

**Estimand and decision rule:** The primary value is the Shapley-attributed fraction of total squared remission/resistant group-mean expression distance assigned to composition. “Composition-dominant” means a point estimate above 0.50 with donor-level uncertainty and held-out state assignment sufficiently stable to support that direction. This threshold is a descriptive criterion, not a clinical decision threshold. Report the component magnitudes as well as the share, because ratios can be unstable if total distance is near zero. Do not silently redefine the gene set, clustering resolution, or split after seeing the desired direction; report sensitivity as exploratory and require any selected alternative to be identified as exploratory.

## Outcomes, falsification, and next decisions

- **Supportive:** technical/status overlap passes the prespecified gate; held-out state mappings and donor influence are stable; the composition share is above 0.50 with donor-level uncertainty supporting a dominant direction. This supports only a cross-sectional decomposition of selected, captured macrophages. Continue to spatial/cell-count validation and clinical adjudication; do not say state abundance causes remission.
- **Adverse:** a precise and stable result assigns at least as much distance to within-state expression as to composition, or the composition result reverses under donor holdout/state mapping checks. This weakens this cohort’s composition-dominant hypothesis and redirects the next study toward validating within-state programs or other measured alternatives. It does not establish a particular pathway or mechanism.
- **Inconclusive/defer:** wide donor-level intervals, low state-map stability, small/near-zero total distance, status/technical non-overlap, dominant donor leverage, or lack of sufficient state support in one group. This means the dataset cannot separate the explanations reliably; it is not decisive evidence for equality or against a biological effect. Obtain better-resolved clinical metadata, independent donor replication, spatial/whole-tissue measurement or a prospective design before advancing.

**Exact evidence needed beyond this analysis:** Clinician review of remission/resistance definitions, assessment date, disease-activity score, drug class/dose/duration and prior treatment trajectory, biopsy indication/selection, and donor-level covariates to distinguish severity and treatment history; independent pathology or spatial measurement to determine whether captured state proportions reflect tissue localization/abundance; and prospective/perturbational evidence to claim state transitions, mechanism, or treatment causality. Computationally checkable outputs include joins/cohort counts, cell/run yield summaries, state-fit reproducibility, effect/decomposition calculations, donor-level uncertainty and whether conclusions follow those outputs. Clinical label validity, unrecorded severity/treatment confounding, mechanisms, and treatment effects require adjudication or another study; an automatic verifier cannot establish them.

## Key references

[K1] Alivernini S, et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” *Nature Medicine* (2020). DOI: 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Abstract-only inspection. The prior supports subset heterogeneity/remission association, not causation or the proposed decomposition. The proposed contribution is an explicit donor-aware component attribution plus technical-overlap gate in the bound contrast.

[K2] Kuo D, et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” *Science Translational Medicine* (2019). DOI: 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only inspection. This supports a within-state and macrophage–fibroblast rival; the present macrophage-only assay cannot establish or localize that crosstalk.

[K3] De Lima J, et al. “Spatial mapping of rheumatoid arthritis synovial niches reveals a LYVE1+ macrophage network associated with response to therapy.” *Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases* (2025). DOI: 10.1016/j.ard.2025.07.019. Abstract-only inspection. This supports spatial/treatment timing as a material boundary; the current single-biopsy profiles cannot test their longitudinal or spatial claims.

Do not include healthy, untreated/naive RA, undifferentiated arthritis, or SA149/SA149P related-or-repeated identity records in this primary contrast. One donor is the independent unit; cells and sequencing runs are not independent biological replicates.

**Prepared profile and annotations:** `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz` (SHA-256 `95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36`) has feature-by-sample expression (`feature` row identifier, sample IDs as columns; 33,694 feature rows and 27 samples per assay registry). `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json` (SHA-256 `4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da`) has 27 sample records and fields `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `other_donor_id`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata`, `source_name`, and `cells`. Join matrix columns to `sample_id` exactly. Filter verified rows on `tissue='synovial membrane'`, `cell_type='macrophage'`, RA disease and remission/resistance response; verify rather than infer from abbreviated labels. Preserve the prepared table for simple baseline only after checking its transformation/scale; it has no cell-state assignments.

**Primary single-cell inputs for decomposition:** For each of the 13 named donor prefixes, use the exact source trio `[private-path]/{prefix}.matrix.mtx`, `{prefix}.genes.tsv`, and `{prefix}.barcodes.tsv`, where prefixes are `RemSA132`, `RemSA159`, `RemSA160`, `RemSA161`, `RemSA168`, `RemSA174`, `RemSA225`, `ResistantSA144`, `ResistantSA145`, `ResistantSA151`, `ResistantSA166`, `ResistantSA222`, and `ResistantSA227`. The MEX-like sparse matrix is genes/features by cells; matrix row i maps to row i of that donor’s `genes.tsv`, and column j maps to row j of its `barcodes.tsv`. Use the same donor identity for all three files; do not join unrelated dataset ID namespaces. Verify matrix orientation, count scale, dimensions and feature concordance against source files before fitting. These are the assay’s available cell profiles, not a download of FASTQ/BAM or spatial data. No cluster labels are available in the bound files; infer them as part of the alternative.

**Run/protocol reconciliation and time boundary:** `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.sdrf.txt` (SHA-256 `b87005a9eefff1beb2d12de2e9f945e2a0b6330aa59207f61f0ecaba180fa237`) is a 106-row run-level design with columns including `Source Name`, `Characteristics[individual]`, `Characteristics[disease]`, `Characteristics[response to treatment]`, `Characteristics[age]`, `Characteristics[sex]`, `Characteristics[organism part]`, `Characteristics[cell type]`, `Characteristics[disease staging]`, `Technology Type`, `Comment[ENA_EXPERIMENT]`, `Scan Name`, `Comment[ENA_RUN]`, `Comment[LIBRARY_LAYOUT]`, `Comment[LIBRARY_STRATEGY]`, and `Derived Array Data File`. Join its `Source Name` to design `source_name`; cross-check `Characteristics[individual]` and status before comparing runs per donor. These are technical sequencing-run/library records, not independent subjects. `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.idf.txt` (SHA-256 `3755fdf0db73c3dca32e0b4b70aeec2e91df16a737137933de2064aeb1bfe069`) lists experiment metadata and an experiment date of 2018-08-01; there is no per-donor pre/post timeline. Restrict inference to one sampled biopsy per donor and the deposited response labels. Do not analyze change over time or imply treatment caused status.

## Analysis plan and method comparison

First, reconcile donor/status mappings and inspect overlap between response group and observable technical variables (run count, ENA experiment/assay, platform/library fields if variable), along with age, sex, captured-cell yield, and sample-processing descriptors available in the design/SDRF. Show complete donor-level tables and standardized differences rather than relying on a regression coefficient with n=13. Quantify RNA/cell recovery and library-depth dependence. Technical variables that are constant across groups cannot be adjusted; if status is perfectly confounded with an observable processing/run variable, stop biological attribution and report non-identifiability. Cell yields characterize sampling precision, not population abundance in tissue.

**Baseline:** aggregate all captured macrophage expression per donor from the bound single-cell matrix, then estimate remission-minus-resistant differences for common expressed genes after library-size normalization and a fixed variance-stabilizing transformation. Confirm direction and donor influence with the prepared donor profile as a scale/lineage sensitivity check. Use equal donor weighting; uncertainty comes from donor bootstrap and donor-label permutation (up to all 1,716 assignments of 7 labels among 13), never from treating cells as replicates. The baseline determines whether an all-cell average difference is present but cannot say why.

**Alternative selected:** cross-fitted donor-level state decomposition using the original per-cell profiles. In leave-one-donor-out folds, learn low-dimensional structure and macrophage expression-state clusters on the other donors, map the held-out donor’s cells to learned states, and align fold-specific state labels by marker/centroid similarity. Report held-out state assignment and mapping stability; the hypothesis is not interpretable if state maps do not reproduce. Estimate a donor’s state-proportion vector and state-conditional gene profile, then compute standardized group means and the composition-versus-within-state contribution to squared multigene expression distance using symmetric Shapley allocation (the composition-by-expression interaction split equally). Restrict the primary feature set to genes detected in both groups under a label-blind donor/cell prevalence filter fixed before status comparisons. Use identical donors, genes, normalization and equal-donor group weights for baseline and decomposition. Bootstrap and permute donors; report uncertainty and all leave-one-donor-out results. Do not make cell-level significance claims or use learned states as treatment predictors.

The method-comparison rationale, targets, split, uncertainty approach and CPU budget are recorded separately in `method-comparison.md`. The decomposition is selected because it could attribute an observed average difference to two biologically distinct statistical components; no neural embedding or GPU is necessary for this small, donor-limited question. Cross-fitting limits donor leakage but cannot make expression-defined clusters independent of the biological contrast or eliminate capture confounding.

**Estimand and decision rule:** The primary value is the Shapley-attributed fraction of total squared remission/resistant group-mean expression distance assigned to composition. “Composition-dominant” means a point estimate above 0.50 with donor-level uncertainty and held-out state assignment sufficiently stable to support that direction. This threshold is a descriptive criterion, not a clinical decision threshold. Report the component magnitudes as well as the share, because ratios can be unstable if total distance is near zero. Do not silently redefine the gene set, clustering resolution, or split after seeing the desired direction; report sensitivity as exploratory and require any selected alternative to be identified as exploratory.

## Outcomes, falsification, and next decisions

- **Supportive:** technical/status overlap passes the prespecified gate; held-out state mappings and donor influence are stable; the composition share is above 0.50 with donor-level uncertainty supporting a dominant direction. This supports only a cross-sectional decomposition of selected, captured macrophages. Continue to spatial/cell-count validation and clinical adjudication; do not say state abundance causes remission.
- **Adverse:** a precise and stable result assigns at least as much distance to within-state expression as to composition, or the composition result reverses under donor holdout/state mapping checks. This weakens this cohort’s composition-dominant hypothesis and redirects the next study toward validating within-state programs or other measured alternatives. It does not establish a particular pathway or mechanism.
- **Inconclusive/defer:** wide donor-level intervals, low state-map stability, small/near-zero total distance, status/technical non-overlap, dominant donor leverage, or lack of sufficient state support in one group. This means the dataset cannot separate the explanations reliably; it is not decisive evidence for equality or against a biological effect. Obtain better-resolved clinical metadata, independent donor replication, spatial/whole-tissue measurement or a prospective design before advancing.

**Exact evidence needed beyond this analysis:** Clinician review of remission/resistance definitions, assessment date, disease-activity score, drug class/dose/duration and prior treatment trajectory, biopsy indication/selection, and donor-level covariates to distinguish severity and treatment history; independent pathology or spatial measurement to determine whether captured state proportions reflect tissue localization/abundance; and prospective/perturbational evidence to claim state transitions, mechanism, or treatment causality. Computationally checkable outputs include joins/cohort counts, cell/run yield summaries, state-fit reproducibility, effect/decomposition calculations, donor-level uncertainty and whether conclusions follow those outputs. Clinical label validity, unrecorded severity/treatment confounding, mechanisms, and treatment effects require adjudication or another study; an automatic verifier cannot establish them.

## Key references

[K1] Alivernini S, et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” *Nature Medicine* (2020). DOI: 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Abstract-only inspection. The prior supports subset heterogeneity/remission association, not causation or the proposed decomposition. The proposed contribution is an explicit donor-aware component attribution plus technical-overlap gate in the bound contrast.

[K2] Kuo D, et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” *Science Translational Medicine* (2019). DOI: 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only inspection. This supports a within-state and macrophage–fibroblast rival; the present macrophage-only assay cannot establish or localize that crosstalk.

[K3] De Lima J, et al. “Spatial mapping of rheumatoid arthritis synovial niches reveals a LYVE1+ macrophage network associated with response to therapy.” *Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases* (2025). DOI: 10.1016/j.ard.2025.07.019. Abstract-only inspection. This supports spatial/treatment timing as a material boundary; the current single-biopsy profiles cannot test their longitudinal or spatial claims.
